freeze.event: The merge commit on main of the PR that adds this file. Every execution record names protocolVersion and the SHA-256 of this file; the decider rejects a record made under any other protocol bytes.
executedInG2: dotnet test --list-tests (enumerates names; runs no test) for Calor.Verification.Tests and Calor.Compiler.Tests at the registration base plus the G2 change, to freeze cases.json.

Only the testName fields of the ordinary-CI TRX files of run 37137354219 (verification and compiler shards) were read, to confirm that the listed names equal the names a test run reports. No outcome field was read.
The unit test DeterminismRecordWritesCompactCellsAndExactGeneratedBytes (a writer test with a synthetic cell; it runs no verifier).

A control-mode dry run of a first harness draft on pull request #1479 (run 37142264571, 13 runner-minutes, charged to determinism-compute): Calor.Semantics.Tests, not a registered case, on all five environments. It confirmed the runner labels, logical processor counts, the private SDK/runtime root, and the empty ~/.calor on every environment. The harness draft it ran is not the registered one.
notExecutedInG2: No registered case was run under this protocol, and no attempt record of a registered case exists.
The release-critical oracle CommittedReportsMatchGeneratedOracle was not run by G2 outside the ordinary CI checks of the G2 pull request, and no per-cell record was produced or inspected.

cases.deterministicSet: Every case in cases.json: every registered test name (with its multiplicity) of every group, every oracle cell, and every oracle artifact.
cases.timingSensitiveRule: The set is empty and the validator keeps it empty (D011): the decider gives a timing-sensitive case no semantics, so a non-empty set could only weaken the registration. Adding the semantics (such a case is still run and retained, never establishes anything, never resolves a row, and no release-critical gate may carry it) is a protocol amendment with a reviewed #1407 amendment, followed by a complete new execution. A Z3 timeout that changes a verdict is verdict instability, not an allowance.

caseKeys.test: test:<group>:<display name>. Display names can repeat (truncated theory arguments), so a test case is the name with its registered multiplicity, and its value in an attempt is the sorted list of TRX outcomes for that name.
caseKeys.cell: cell:<case id> for each of the 1,170 F-4 matrix cells. Its value is the SHA-256 (first 32 hex digits) of the cell's CaseResult object re-serialized with sorted keys; every field, including detail, is compared.
caseKeys.artifact: artifact:<name>. The two oracle reports (value: SHA-256 of the exact generated bytes; pass value: SHA-256 of the committed file's raw bytes) and translator-fixture (value: SHA-256 of '<fixture hash>|<SemanticsVersion>' written by TranslatorOutputMatchesCommittedBaseline before it asserts; pass value: the same over the committed constants), so two different failing translator outputs are a DISAGREE, not one AGREE-FAIL.
caseKeys.invocation: invocation:<profile> for each profile. Its value is '<exit code>|<TRX ResultSummary outcome>' ('timeout|...' when killed). Pass value: '0|Completed'. A test run that fails or aborts as a whole cannot contribute all-Passed values unnoticed.

cases.cellRule: A cell record must have exactly cellFields with their CaseResult types; a missing, extra, or mistyped field, an unregistered or duplicate id, or an identity that differs from the registry makes the value Malformed and the record INVALID.

gateSites: test.yml job 'test' step 'Run verifier-runtime differential gate' (required check 'test')

toolchain.installRoot: The dotnet-install script bundled with actions/setup-dotnet v4 (pinned by commit and SHA-256), run with only toolchain.sdk into an empty private directory under the runner temp directory, so the dotnet root holds exactly one SDK and one Microsoft.NETCore.App runtime. Preinstalled SDKs are not on the path (amendment 1.1.0; the original text named setup-dotnet).
toolchain.build: dotnet build <project> -c Release, once per job, before the first attempt. Attempts run dotnet test --no-build.

randomSeed.effect: Amendment 1.2.0 (found in the #1135 repair review): Z3 4.15.7 rejects random_seed as a context parameter (it prints "unknown parameter 'random_seed'" and ignores it), so the constant has never reached the solver and every context runs with Z3's default seed. The pin still freezes the tree's constant; the effective solver configuration is the Z3 defaults plus the per-check timeout. Applying the seed would change every Z3-backed test's search and is not done.

z3.rule: The harness never overrides a Z3 parameter. The seed and per-case timeout are properties of the tree; the validator checks them against these values, so a change to either is a protocol amendment. Amendment 1.2.0: the seed constant is pinned but not applied by Z3 (randomSeed.effect).

checkout.rule: Every environment checks out the committed bytes (git config --global core.autocrlf false before checkout). Inputs are byte-identical on every platform, so any platform difference comes from the code under test. This is an input pin, not a normalization: no output is ever converted. Tracked files must be unmodified before the first attempt and after every invocation (git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no is empty); otherwise that invocation and every later attempt in the job are invalid.

parallelism.xunit: Project defaults. At registration no test project under tests/ has an xunit.runner.json or a .runsettings file; the validator fails if one appears in a registered project directory.
parallelism.attempts: Attempts in a job run one after another. Each invocation is a fresh dotnet test process and test host.
parallelism.jobs: Jobs of one execution may run concurrently on separate runners.

perInvocation: Each invocation runs with HOME, USERPROFILE, and DOTNET_CLI_HOME set to a fresh directory under the job's own output directory (NUGET_PACKAGES pinned explicitly to the path the build step used), so the verifier's user-level cache starts empty and the real home directory is never read, written, or deleted. Harness files may not look up the real home directory at all (validator: home_safe, D013).
Remove every CALOR_UPDATE_* variable from the invocation environment, so no test rewrites a committed baseline.
Set CALOR_Z3_EXPECTED_RID to the environment's RID and CALOR_DETERMINISM_RECORD_DIR to a fresh directory for the invocation.

environmentRule: Platform (OS and RID) is a determinism dimension (contract rules.platformDeterminism). Every supported RID in eng/z3-consumers.json is a registered environment. compiler-verifier runs on linux-x64 only, the only platform its release gates use; the protocol establishes nothing for it on another platform and says so in every result. Runner labels are pinned (no -latest label). The runner image version cannot be pinned on hosted runners; every attempt records ImageOS and ImageVersion, and a disagreement is never excused by an image change.

runPlan.attemptOrder: Within an attempt, profiles run in the order listed in profiles[], filtered to the environment's profiles.
runPlan.stoppingRule: An execution runs every registered attempt in every environment. Nothing stops early, on agreement or on disagreement. A job that ends early (job timeout, runner loss, harness defect) leaves its remaining attempts recorded as infrastructure-failure or invalid; they are retained and make the execution INCOMPLETE.
runPlan.statisticalBound: With zero disagreement in an execution, the one-sided 95% upper bound on the per-attempt disagreement probability is about 1 - 0.05^(1/n): about 9.5% per environment (n = 30) and about 2.0% across the 150 attempts of a Calor.Verification.Tests case. compiler-verifier has n = 30 on linux-x64 only. The protocol bounds non-determinism; it does not prove its absence.
runPlan.harnessCutInconsistency: Known inconsistency, left unchanged by amendment 1.3.0: stoppingRule says a job that ends early makes the execution INCOMPLETE, but an invocation the harness itself cuts at the job deadline is recorded with the value Timeout for every unobserved case (attemptStatuses.timeout), and values of invalid attempts are compared, so such a cut makes those cases DISAGREE (NON-DETERMINISTIC). In g3-exec-1 every DISAGREE came from such cuts on Windows. Amendment 1.3.0 removes the cause (Windows job time) and keeps the decider unchanged.

agreement.rule: A case agrees only when every expected contribution is present and every contribution has the identical value, across all attempts, jobs, profiles, and environments of the execution. One differing contribution makes the case DISAGREE.

passValue.test: Every outcome in the sorted list is Passed, with exactly the registered multiplicity.
passValue.cell: The cell's mismatch field is false.
passValue.artifact: Report artifacts: the SHA-256 of the committed file's raw bytes. translator-fixture: the SHA-256 of the committed '<ExpectedFixtureHash>|<ExpectedSemanticsVersion>'.

agreement.normalizationStatement: No normalization is applied to any compared value. Line endings, encodings, whitespace, case, and ordering inside a value are compared exactly. CRLF is never converted. A difference caused only by line endings is a DISAGREE (or AGREE-FAIL) and is resolved by making the bytes platform-independent, never by a rule here or a per-platform baseline.

projections.reason: Timing, host, and message text are not verdicts. The verdict of a test is its outcome.
Each cell object is parsed and re-serialized with sorted keys before hashing; no field is dropped or changed.

attemptStatuses.completed: Every profile invocation of the attempt finished within its process timeout and produced a TRX file. Test failures are data, not a status.
attemptStatuses.timeout: A profile invocation hit its process timeout and was killed. Every case of that profile without a result gets the value Timeout.
attemptStatuses.crash: A profile invocation exited without a TRX file or with fewer results than registered. Missing cases get the value Crash or Missing.
attemptStatuses.infrastructure-failure: The attempt never started a test invocation because a setup step failed (checkout, SDK, Z3 bootstrap, environment check, or build) or the job ended before it. No case value.
attemptStatuses.environment-violation: The environment check failed (SDK, runtime, OS, architecture, processor count, Z3 asset hash, commit, autocrlf, or a dirty tree). The attempt is retained and contributes no case value.
attemptStatuses.invalid: The record is malformed, the harness failed after starting, the tree was modified by an earlier invocation, or an unregistered case or cell appeared. No case value; an unregistered case makes the execution INVALID.

valueRules.skipped: Skipped and NotExecuted are outcomes. They are never Passed, so a skipped case never agrees as a pass.
valueRules.unavailable: Z3 unavailable makes the guard facts and the oracle fail (they fail rather than skip); those failures are outcomes.
valueRules.timeout: Timeout and Crash are values. They never equal Passed and are never converted to agreement.
valueRules.missingContribution: An expected contribution with no value (infrastructure-failure, environment-violation, or a missing record) is not a value. Values from an invalid attempt are compared, so they can reveal a DISAGREE, but they never count toward agreement: a case with an invalid contribution is at best INCOMPLETE.

caseClasses.AGREE-PASS: Every expected contribution present, all identical, equal to the pass value. The only class that establishes determinism for a case.
caseClasses.AGREE-FAIL: Every expected contribution present and identical, but not the pass value. Deterministically failing; release-blocking as a failing gate.
caseClasses.DISAGREE: At least two different values among the contributions present. Non-deterministic: release-blocking for the affected modeled form or artifact until resolved under contract section 8. platformDependent is true when each environment is internally constant but environments differ.
caseClasses.INCOMPLETE: No disagreement among the values present, but at least one expected contribution is missing. Not established.

executionVerdicts.INVALID: A record is malformed or internally inconsistent (status, exit code, invocation, and values; environment attestation), made under other protocol or harness bytes, from another commit or run id, from an unregistered environment, job, or attempt, duplicated, from a re-run job (GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT > 1), contains an unregistered case or cell, or more than one execution is passed to the decider.
executionVerdicts.FAILING: No DISAGREE, and any case is AGREE-FAIL.
executionVerdicts.INCOMPLETE: No DISAGREE and no AGREE-FAIL, but a case is INCOMPLETE.
executionVerdicts.DETERMINISTIC: Every registered case is AGREE-PASS. The only verdict that establishes determinism, and only for the registered environments and profiles.

failureRules: Any DISAGREE case is non-deterministic and release-blocking for the affected form, test, or artifact until resolved under contract section 8 (fixed, or visibly demoted under #1413). Deselecting it on a platform is never a resolution.

No attempt is excluded, re-classified, or replaced after it ran. Every attempt record, including infrastructure failures, is retained, and every value an invocation observed is kept: only an unobserved value is filled.
A commit is executed at most once. A later execution on another commit never erases an earlier one; the ledger and every result stay reported.
The final determination is the single execution on the final commit, and it must be DETERMINISTIC.
A determinism row is resolved only when every case mapped to it is AGREE-PASS in an execution that ran every environment the row names.
The decider binds every record to the expected full commit SHA and to the run id of its execution; a record from another commit, run, or re-run attempt makes the execution INVALID.

retryPolicy.rule: No attempt, job, workflow run, or commit is run again. GitHub's re-run is rejected: the decider rejects any record with GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT other than 1 (INVALID). A commit is executed at most once in execution mode, whatever its verdict; the next execution needs a different commit. After NON-DETERMINISTIC or FAILING, that commit must differ from the previous one in at least one path outside docs/ (checked with git by the execution machinery) and the ledger names the repair and the cases it addresses. Every execution stays reported.

determinismRows.source: artifact-inventory.json verifier-runtime-differential openDefects (#1135: runs 33137941806 success and 33139062112 failure on commit 04b32afa)

budget.accounting: Runner-minutes are the sum over every job of every determinism-protocol run charged here, each job's duration (completed_at - started_at from the GitHub API) rounded up to a whole minute, with no OS multiplier. #1135 records them in the ledger.

charges.determinism-compute: Every workflow_dispatch run of the protocol workflow, in execution or control mode, by anyone. The execution machinery counts them from the GitHub API run inventory (not from a hand-written ledger) and reserves the worst case of every unfinished run before starting a new one.
charges.ordinary-ci: Control-mode runs started by pull_request on the workflow or harness paths (they run no registered case).
charges.openQuestion: #1424's execution on the frozen candidate is charged to determinism-compute under this rule, and 3 executions plus 2 control runs leave 105 runner-minutes, less than one execution. Charging it to regeneration-compute needs an amendment that binds that charge to the #1423 candidate. Amendment 1.3.0: with the Windows job timeouts at 75 minutes and no dispatched control run, 3 executions reach 1,965 runner-minutes in the worst case; contract amendment 1.2.0 charges #1424's candidate-time execution to regeneration-compute.

budget.rule: The execution machinery refuses to start a run when recorded minutes plus the worst case of every unfinished run plus this run's worst case exceed the ceiling, or when maxExecutions or maxDispatchedControlRuns is reached. Reaching a limit is contract stopping rule 1: stop, record the overrun, and either merge an amendment raising the ceiling or record the gate BLOCKED.
budget.amendment130: Execution g3-exec-1 (run 37177387101) spent 388 runner-minutes, so 13 + 388 = 401 are recorded. Its Windows jobs took 46 minutes (about 6 minutes of setup and about 3.1 minutes per attempt) and the harness stopped them at 45 minutes (50 minus 5). Raising win-x64 and win-arm64 to 75 minutes makes the worst case per execution 5 + 10 + 2 x (70 + 50 + 50 + 75 + 75) = 655, and 3 x 655 = 1,965 <= 2,000 only with maxDispatchedControlRuns 0 (no control run was ever dispatched). Worst case of the two executions left: 401 + 2 x 655 = 1,711.

executions.retention: Actions artifacts (90 days) are a transport, not storage. #1135 commits, per execution, result.json and a gzip tarball of every attempt record, with their SHA-256 values in the ledger.
executions.ledgerCheck: Every workflow_dispatch run of the protocol workflow (from the paginated GitHub API inventory) must appear in the ledger with its measured runner-minutes (non-negative, from job timestamps); a missing run fails the check.

workflow.rule: The execution machinery (workflow, environment check, attempt runner, plan with budget, history, and amendment guards) was added by the second G2 PR and registered by amendment 1.1.0, which set status to registered and froze its files (D015). D013 checks the workflow's structure (workflow_problems: triggers, inputs, jobs, steps, commands, conditions), rejects any other workflow that runs the runner, and checks that no harness file looks up the real home directory. Changing either file is a protocol amendment.
requirements: Jobs plan -> attempts matrix -> decide. fail-fast false; no continue-on-error, no masked exit status; runner labels, timeouts, and SDK from this file.
Exact SDK and runtime installed into a private dotnet root by a procedure that installs nothing else; the environment check rejects any other SDK or Microsoft.NETCore.App runtime.
Each attempt record written after every profile invocation, so a later failure cannot discard earlier observations; a TRX that exists after a timeout is still read.

plan validates this protocol against the packet on protected main (D016), refuses a commit already executed, refuses a repair that changes only docs/, and enforces the budget from the API run inventory.
decide receives the dispatched commit SHA and the run id; records from any other commit or run are INVALID.
Pull-request runs are control mode only.

Absolute paths for every record directory passed to a test host, and an isolated HOME/USERPROFILE under the job temp directory for every invocation; no code path deletes or writes the real home directory.
implementation: Jobs plan -> attempts matrix -> decide, each starting with the same step that refuses GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT other than 1 before any action runs. fail-fast false; no continue-on-error, ||, or set +e (D013); runner labels and job timeouts come from this file through the plan matrix; plan and decide timeouts equal budget.planJobTimeoutMinutes and decideJobTimeoutMinutes.

install-sdk downloads the dotnet-install script bundled with actions/setup-dotnet v4 (commit 67a3573c), checks its pinned SHA-256, and runs it with only the toolchain.sdk version into an empty private root under the runner temp directory. env-check records an environment-violation unless dotnet resolves inside that root (path components, case-insensitive on Windows) and it lists exactly toolchain.sdk and exactly one Microsoft.NETCore.App runtime, toolchain.runtime.

run-job writes the attempt record (status invalid, reason 'attempt in progress') after every profile invocation and the final record when the attempt ends, by atomic replace. A TRX that exists after a timeout is read; unreadable record files keep the TRX values and make the invocation invalid. run-job starts no invocation, and cuts a running one, 5 minutes before the job timeout (from the job's start time), so fill-missing and the upload run; unrun attempts are recorded invalid (harness started), environment-violation, or infrastructure-failure (setup failed). An existing record is never replaced.

plan runs this tree's validator and main's validator against origin/main (D016) and reads the paginated GitHub API inventory of every run of the workflow (all branches and run attempts; a missing total_count, short read, or duplicate fails closed). It refuses: a non-dispatch event; GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT other than 1; a GITHUB_WORKFLOW_REF other than this workflow, or a run not listed in its inventory under its own title; a reused execution id; a ledger run missing from the inventory; a commit any earlier execution-mode run started attempts on (or the ledger records as executed), or an unfinished execution; after an execution run that did not conclude success, a commit whose diff from that run's commit (NUL-separated names) touches only docs/; and a run for which dryRunSpent plus every dispatched run's measured minutes (the larger of API and ledger) plus the worst case of every unfinished run plus this run's worst case exceed ceilingRunnerMinutes, or that would exceed maxExecutions (runs that started attempts) or maxDispatchedControlRuns (every dispatched control run).

decide passes the dispatched commit (GITHUB_SHA) and the run id (GITHUB_RUN_ID) to the frozen decider and downloads only run-attempt-1 artifacts; every machinery command refuses GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT other than 1 and a foreign GITHUB_WORKFLOW_REF.
The workflow has no pull_request (or any other automatic) trigger, so no pull-request run exists; D013 rejects any trigger other than workflow_dispatch.

The first step of every job moves HOME, USERPROFILE, DOTNET_CLI_HOME, APPDATA, LOCALAPPDATA, XDG_*, TEMP, TMP, TMPDIR, the NuGet HTTP, plugin, and scratch caches, the global VCS config, and NUGET_PACKAGES under the runner temp directory. Every test invocation then gets HOME, USERPROFILE, and DOTNET_CLI_HOME set to one fresh, empty directory under the job's output directory with the same per-user and temp roots inside it, an absolute CALOR_DETERMINISM_RECORD_DIR, the build step's NUGET_PACKAGES, CALOR_Z3_EXPECTED_RID, no CALOR_UPDATE_* variable, and MSBUILDDISABLENODEREUSE=1; check_isolation fails closed otherwise.
deviations: toolchain.installRoot named setup-dotnet, which installs a floating LTS runtime and CLI before the requested SDK; the machinery runs setup-dotnet's own pinned install script with only the SDK version instead (workflow.requirements: installs nothing else).

Stricter than retryPolicy: the API does not expose a prior verdict, so every execution run that did not conclude success is treated as possibly NON-DETERMINISTIC or FAILING, and the next execution needs a commit that changes a path outside docs/.

Stricter than budget.charges: a dispatched run with a title the plan cannot read is charged and counted as an execution. A dispatched execution-mode run whose attempts never started (refused by plan, or replaced in the concurrency queue) is charged its minutes but is not an execution.

Added checks: env-check builds and runs a probe app on the pinned runtime with an isolated HOME/USERPROFILE and records whether the root of the verifier's default user-level cache follows it; false is an environment-violation. Amendment 1.2.0: the probe compiles the verifier's own resolver, UserHome.Resolve in src/Calor.Compiler/Verification/Z3/Cache/VerificationCacheOptions.cs (used by VerificationCacheOptions and the user effect-manifest loader), from the checked-out tree, instead of printing SpecialFolder.UserProfile, which on Windows comes from the account's known folder and ignores USERPROFILE. The decider re-judges every attempt's observations (amendment 1.1.0 to _record_problem) and rejects an invocation whose home already held .calor, so an attestation cannot contradict its observations.

Contract amendment 1.2.0 (capacity.chargeRules c2-candidate-determinism-protocol, merged after protocol 1.0.0) charges #1424's candidate-time execution to regeneration-compute when its commit is the #1423 candidate and #1424's regeneration ledger records it. Neither the manifest nor that ledger exists yet, so plan cannot verify a qualifying run: it charges every dispatched run to determinism-compute (over-counting, fail closed). Excluding a qualifying run from that count needs a protocol amendment that names those files; until then reaching a limit is contract stopping rule 1.

Amendment 1.3.0: run-job removes each invocation's isolated home after recording it, fill-missing removes any home an interrupted invocation left and fails when a path that actions/upload-artifact rejects remains, and the home probe builds beside the job's output directory instead of inside it. In g3-exec-1 NuGet cache files named with ':' under those homes made upload-artifact reject the whole artifact of every Linux and macOS job, so their records were never uploaded.
workflow.residual: Runner-minutes for a plan job are spent before plan can refuse, so dispatches after the ceiling still cost up to planJobTimeoutMinutes each; they are charged and visible in the inventory. A run deleted before #1135 records it in the ledger leaves no history. A dispatched ref whose workflow or runner bytes differ produces records whose harnessSha256 main's decider rejects; review and the ledger are the controls for anything else.

recordFormats.decideInputs: Every attempt record of the execution, the execution id with its run id, the dispatched full commit SHA, and the mode.
recordFormats.harnessSha256: Amendment 1.1.0: SHA-256 over 'path sha256' lines of scripts/determinism_protocol.py, scripts/determinism_runner.py, and .github/workflows/determinism-protocol.yml (harness_digest).

amendments.rule: Any change after merge to the frozen files (sha256.json, D015) is a new protocolVersion with an appended amendmentLog entry (UTC timestamp, reviewed PR, justification, whether it follows a decision-bearing execution); earlier entries are immutable. The required calor-first-guard job runs main's copy of the validator (the trusted entry point) and this tree's copy against the packet on protected main (D016): an unrecorded change, or one that removes a case, environment, determinism row, or attempt, fails. An amendment that follows a decision-bearing execution is followed by a complete new execution on a new commit. Moving a case between the deterministic and timing-sensitive sets also needs a #1407 amendment. Every attempt record carries the SHA-256 of protocol.json and of the harness; the decider rejects records made under other bytes. D016 compares the contribution matrix (every case's expected contributions per environment, with test multiplicity) and each determinism row's cases and environments; any reduction fails. A baseline ref that does not resolve, or a partial packet on it, fails closed.

amendmentLog.justification: Registers the execution machinery required by workflow.requirements (the second G2 PR): .github/workflows/determinism-protocol.yml and scripts/determinism_runner.py, frozen by sha256.json. Records how each requirement is implemented (workflow.implementation), the deviations (pinned installer instead of setup-dotnet; stricter repair and charge rules; an added home probe and attestation re-check in the decider; harnessSha256 binding the runner and workflow; contract 1.2.0's #1424 charge rule not yet applied by plan, which over-counts), the residual, and one limitation. No case, environment, attempt, determinism row, gate, agreement rule, or budget value changes. No registered case was run.

#1135 repair, before any execution. On Windows, SpecialFolder.UserProfile comes from the account's known folder and ignores USERPROFILE, so the registered home probe would have recorded every win-x64 and win-arm64 attempt as an environment-violation, and no execution could resolve the three Windows determinism rows. The verifier now resolves its user-level root through UserHome.Resolve (USERPROFILE on Windows when set and fully qualified; SpecialFolder.UserProfile otherwise, unchanged on Linux and macOS), and env-check's probe compiles that resolver from the tree under test instead of asking the runtime. It also records that the registered seed constant is not applied (Z3 rejects random_seed as a context parameter; z3.randomSeed.applied false), which changes no behavior. Changes scripts/determinism_runner.py (the probe), scripts/test_determinism_protocol.py (a control that the probe compiles the tree's resolver), the deviation and limitation texts, and the README. No case, environment, attempt, determinism row, gate, agreement rule, record format, or budget value changes. No decision-bearing protocol execution was run; the repair PR ran local and ordinary-CI tests.

After execution g3-exec-1 (run 37177387101, commit 0142438f, NON-DETERMINISTIC, complete false). Two machinery defects, not verifier findings: (1) the Linux and macOS jobs (6 of 10) ran every attempt, but upload-artifact rejected their output directories because the home probe's and the invocations' NuGet HTTP caches hold file names with ':'; (2) the Windows jobs needed more than the 45 minutes the harness allows under a 50-minute job timeout, and the cut invocations' Timeout values made 1,580 cases DISAGREE. Every value a completed Windows invocation observed equals the pass value. Repairs: homes are removed before upload and checked by fill-missing; the probe builds beside the output directory; win-x64 and win-arm64 jobTimeoutMinutes 50 -> 75; maxDispatchedControlRuns 2 -> 0 so the worst case (3 x 655 = 1,965) stays under the 2,000 ceiling. The decider's treatment of harness-cut invocations is unchanged and recorded as a known inconsistency (runPlan.harnessCutInconsistency). No case, environment, attempt count, determinism row, gate, agreement rule, or record format changes. Per the amendments rule, a complete new execution on a new commit follows.

limitations: Hosted runner images change underneath a pinned label; image versions are recorded, not pinned.
Determinism is established only for the registered environments, profiles, toolchain, and checkout settings. A Windows checkout with core.autocrlf=true is not covered.
compiler-verifier is covered on linux-x64 only.
Thirty attempts per environment bound, but cannot exclude, rare non-determinism (runPlan.statisticalBound).
Theory rows whose display names are identical (truncated arguments) are compared as a multiset of outcomes per name. Any failure among them is detected, but which row failed is not identified.

The home probe checks the verifier's user-home resolver (UserHome.Resolve): USERPROFILE on Windows when set and fully qualified, otherwise SpecialFolder.UserProfile (which follows HOME on Linux and macOS). A user-level path read through any other lookup is not covered; at amendment 1.2.0 the verifier's default cache and the user effect manifests both use the resolver.

Amendment 1.3.0: an invocation cut by the harness's own job-deadline stop yields Timeout values that the decider compares (runPlan.harnessCutInconsistency); job timeouts are sized so this does not happen, but if it does, the execution reads NON-DETERMINISTIC rather than INCOMPLETE.

scope.covered: The release-critical verifier test host (every Calor.Verification.Tests case), the F-4 oracle alone and its 1,170 cells and 2 reports, the translator fixture, and the Calor.Compiler.Tests classes that construct the verifier or Z3 directly (linux-x64).

notCovered.reason: MSBuild-task integration tests that spawn builds; they assert the gate's plumbing, not a verdict of the registered oracle. Ordinary CI runs them once per change.

notCovered.subject: Calor.RoundTrip.Harness.Tests TaskGenAddressabilityTests
notCovered.reason: Asserts that a bug-pattern diagnostic is addressable by a task generator; not a verifier verdict oracle.

notCovered.subject: .github/scripts/test-sdk-package.sh packaged-SDK verifier canary
notCovered.reason: A package-consumer probe of publication, owned by #1410/#1424; it runs on a packed SDK, not on the tree.

scope.rule: Determinism is established only for covered subjects. #1424 and #1408 may not cite this protocol for a notCovered subject; such a subject's single-run result is not established determinism. Adding a subject is an amendment.

resources.rule: Each environment registers its hosted runner class: logical processors (exact) and physical memory in GiB. The environment check records both and records an environment-violation when the processor count differs or physical memory is below 90% of the registered value. Hosted runners cannot cap a process tree's memory; an invocation killed for memory has no TRX and gets the value Crash. Wall-clock limits are the per-profile process timeouts and the job timeouts; a job killed at its timeout leaves its remaining attempts without values (INCOMPLETE).

control.rule: Control mode exercises the workflow and harness on a project that is not registered and runs no verifier oracle. Its case set is what the attempts report. Its verdict is prefixed CONTROL- and is never decision-bearing. Pull-request runs are always control mode.

measurement.rule: The recorder and the CaseResult schema are frozen by sha256.json (D015); the three call sites (DifferentialGate.Run, CommittedReportsMatchGeneratedOracle, TranslatorOutputMatchesCommittedBaseline) must stay (D014). Changing either is a protocol amendment.

gates.rule: D014 parses each workflow (a minimal parser for the job/step subset; no YAML library is available) and requires every gate step below to exist exactly once as its own run step with no if:, no continue-on-error, and no shell override, in a job with no if: or continue-on-error, after its registered earlier steps. A gate with a frozen script must match it line for line, its first command must be 'set -euo pipefail', and each gate command must be a top-level command (not inside if/for/while/case, braces, a subshell, or a heredoc; no ||, &&, ;, &) with no exit, return, set +e, or ERR trap before it. A shard step (a matrix job whose dotnet test runs in a per-shard branch) must start with 'set -euo pipefail', run dotnet test, and contain no '|| true', '|| :', '|| exit 0', or set +e. A later step in the same job that runs after a failure (always(), failure(), cancelled()) must upload artifacts or be registered in alwaysAllowed. Removing or changing a gate is an amendment checked by D016. A shard step's script is frozen by the SHA-256 of its non-blank lines (scriptSha256). Any workflow line at a job or step key position that the parser does not read as a plain key (a quoted key, flow mapping, anchor, or merge key) makes the gate fail.
